# phasetwo_cluster_extension (Resource)

An extension slot on a dedicated cluster — a custom provider, theme or password blacklist.

This registers the slot only. Nothing is deployed until you attach a `phasetwo_cluster_extension_version` carrying the actual file, which is also what triggers the cluster reconcile.

How many extensions a cluster may hold depends on its tier: `starter` allows one theme and no extensions, `premium` one of each, `enterprise` unlimited.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phasetwo_cluster_extension" "custom_authenticator" {
  cluster_id    = phasetwo_cluster.main.id
  name          = "acme-authenticator"
  resource_type = "EXTENSION"
}

resource "phasetwo_cluster_extension" "theme" {
  cluster_id    = phasetwo_cluster.main.id
  name          = "acme-theme"
  resource_type = "THEME"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the cluster.
- `name` (String) Extension name, unique within the cluster.
- `resource_type` (String) What kind of resource this holds:

- `EXTENSION` — a Keycloak provider jar
- `THEME` — a theme jar
- `PASSWORD_BLACKLIST` — a blacklist file

`EXTENSION` and `THEME` are tied to a Keycloak major version, so their versions need `keycloak_major_version`. `PASSWORD_BLACKLIST` is version-independent.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the extension is active. Disabling does not delete its versions.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the extension was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the extension.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import phasetwo_cluster_extension.custom_authenticator 4f8c1e2a-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/2b3c4d5e-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
